title: [epic] HADES silent-failure hardening campaign — fail loud at every boundary
description: Recursive root-cause hardening campaign triggered by the 2026-06-15 blank-enrichment incident (HADES-mcx). Goal: eliminate the CLASS of silent failures where HADES presents degenerate/empty/wrong output as valid, or lets an external-dependency degradation pass unsurfaced. Driven by docs/HARDENING_PROTOCOL.md (self-prompt) with durable state in docs/HARDENING_LEDGER.md. Each child issue = one confirmed silent-failure mode with a force-fail regression test.
design: Loop-until-dry over a prioritized inventory of dependency boundaries and degenerate-data transforms. For each: enumerate failure modes -> trace true root cause (5-whys to a systemic class) -> if silent, force-fail test (RED) + fail-loud fix (GREEN) -> ledger + bead. Stop when 2 consecutive surfaces yield nothing new.
acceptance_criteria: Every external boundary validates content (not just container) and fails loud; force-fail tests cover each mode; a documented convention prevents each class; ledger records audited+ruled-out surfaces; no silent empty/degenerate output reaches display/export/push.

Root cause confirmed: ZoomInfo /enrich/contact returns matched-but-fieldless records (empty data[0]); pipeline silently presents them as valid. Empty enriched object has no id -> search_by_pid backfill misses -> fully blank row -> empty-lead baseline score 64. P2 honest CONTACTS ENRICHED / credits_used counts (exclude empties). P3 score guard for all-identical-baseline result sets.

notes: P0+P1 IMPLEMENTED (TDD, 813 tests pass). P1: zoominfo_client._stamp_requested_pid() carries item['input']['personId'] onto fieldless enrich payloads so geo-page search-backfill restores the lead (real-id-wins invariant tested). title: Add mutation_log table for critical-table writes (data-loss step 3)
description:
Defends against the dominant threat in this codebase: our own code corrupting our own data via buggy mutations (centroid bug, Company Enrich silent failure, phone column inversion all had this shape). Backups don't help here because we back up the bad data right after writing it.

What to do:
- New mutation_log table: id, ts, actor (user/script), table_name, row_id, op (insert/update/delete), before_json, after_json
- Add a tiny LogMutationMixin in db/_mutation_log.py with log_mutation() helper
- Instrument the high-value mutation sites: operators (create/update/delete), staged_exports (insert/mark_exported/mark_pushed), lead_outcomes (update). NOT every table — just the ones where surprise mutations cause operator pain.
- Index on (table_name, ts) for cheap recent-history queries
- A retention policy: keep 90 days, purged by the same weekly sweeper from step 2
- Add a Pipeline Health panel showing last 20 mutations + a 'undo' button surface for a future bead

Why: the actual undo button against our own bad writes. Append-only, cheap at our scale (~hundreds of writes/day across 5 operators), genuinely diagnostic when something goes wrong ("what changed on operators table this morning?"). Effort ~4h.

title: Architect data-loss defenses (threat-model driven)
description:
Parent epic for data-loss defenses, scoped from the systems-architect analysis on 2026-05-19 (see CODE_REVIEW_2026-05-18.md follow-up discussion).

Reframing: the dominant data-loss threat in this codebase is NOT cloud-provider failure — it is OUR OWN CODE corrupting OUR OWN DATA via migration bugs, silent-failure writes, accidental deletes. A traditional backup script protects against the rarest threats (account loss, engine crash) and not the common ones (we happily back up the bad data we just wrote).

This epic ships four small, independent defenses that target the actual threat model. Closure: when all 4 children close.

Children:
- Verify Turso PITR + document/test restore procedure
- Add soft-delete to operators + staged_exports
- Add mutation_log capturing successful writes to critical tables
- Add daily diff alert on operators + lead_outcomes baselines

Combined effort ~10h, can be parallelized by table-affinity (mutation_log + soft-delete share migration discipline).

title: Add Zoho CRM dedup check at export time
description: VSDP cross-references every lead against Zoho CRM Deals before export — marks leads already in CRM and adds the Zoho record URL to Import Notes. HADES has export_dedup.py for cross-session dedup but no CRM check. Add Zoho matching at export time to prevent pushing duplicates already being worked in CRM. Reference: VSDP/vanillasoft_automation.py lines 762-874.

value: Streamlit st.file_uploader returns an UploadedFile (BytesIO) that is REUSED across reruns with a RETAINED read position.
